history.label: History
history.seoDescription: History of Rază de Soare Special School in Arad.
history.pageTitle: History of „Rază de Soare” Special School

paragraphs.p1: Rază de Soare Special School was established in response to a real need within the Arad community.
paragraphs.p2: In January 2002, as a response to the need for inclusive and specialized education for children with special educational needs, our institution was founded. The initiative aimed to create a place where children with moderate, severe, and profound intellectual disabilities could follow an adapted educational program in a safe and supportive environment.
paragraphs.p3: The school operates within the Christian Foundation „RCE Speranța Copiilor”, a non-profit organization that supports and promotes social and educational services dedicated to children and families in the community.
paragraphs.p4: Over the years, „Rază de Soare” has steadily developed, offering adapted education for children aged between 3 and 18 years. The program covers kindergarten (starting with the small group) up to the 10th grade, with small class sizes (6–8 students) coordinated by two teachers, ensuring personalized attention and meaningful development for each student.
paragraphs.p5: Throughout time, our mission has extended beyond teaching, becoming a holistic support center that promotes inclusion, personal development, and the dignity of every child.

missionVisionPage.title: Mission & Vision
missionVisionPage.missionLead: Rază de Soare Special School is committed to providing each child with special educational needs a safe, stable, and individualized environment where personal development, autonomy, and communication are fundamental priorities.
missionVisionPage.missionParagraph1: Our activity addresses children and young people with moderate, severe, and profound intellectual disabilities who require structured educational interventions, consistent support, and a framework in which progress is measured through real steps toward independence and social integration.
missionList: development of practical life skills and personal autonomy;
stimulation of functional communication and emotional expression;
building social competencies necessary for community integration;
supporting families through educational partnership and ongoing guidance.
missionVisionPage.missionParagraph2: Small classes of 6–8 students, coordinated by two teachers, allow for personalized approaches and interventions tailored to each child. Emphasis is placed on individual progress, personal rhythm, and valuing every achievement.
missionVisionPage.missionParagraph3: At the heart of our educational mission stands respect for human dignity and the conviction that every child deserves genuine opportunities for development.
missionVisionPage.visionParagraph1: The vision of Rază de Soare Special School is that of an educational community where difference is not a limitation, but a starting point for support, understanding, and growth.
missionVisionPage.visionParagraph2: We envision a society in which children and young people with intellectual disabilities are viewed through the lens of their potential rather than their limitations. A society where inclusion means real participation and integration is supported through adapted education and responsible intervention.
missionVisionPage.visionParagraph3: Within the RCE 'Speranța Copiilor' Foundation, our school promotes values such as respect for life and human dignity, responsibility toward others, compassion, and mutual support.
missionVisionPage.visionParagraph4: We believe true education does not mean standardization, but attentive guidance and continuous support. Every child is unique, and the educational process must respond to that uniqueness.
missionVisionPage.visionParagraph5: Through our work, we aim to contribute to the development of young people who are as autonomous as possible, able to communicate, participate in community life, and build the skills necessary for a more independent life.

teamPage.title: Our Team
teamPage.intro1: The team of Rază de Soare Special School consists of teachers and specialists experienced in working with children with special educational needs. Our activity is based on interdisciplinary collaboration, professional responsibility, and respect for the dignity of every child.
teamPage.intro2: Through individualized approaches and teamwork, we aim to develop autonomy, communication, and practical skills necessary for community integration.

curriculumPage.title: Adapted Curriculum
curriculumPage.lead: The adapted curriculum of Rază de Soare Special School is built upon the real needs of each child. The educational process does not pursue uniform academic performance standards, but the progressive development of autonomy, communication, and functional skills necessary for community integration.
curriculumPage.paragraph1: Each student benefits from an individualized educational plan, adapted to their developmental level, personal learning pace, and cognitive and emotional particularities.

cognitive.title: Cognitive Development
cognitive.text: Stimulation of learning processes through activities adapted to each student's level of understanding.

communication.title: Communication and Language
communication.text: Development of functional communication, verbal or alternative, depending on individual needs.

autonomy.title: Personal Autonomy
autonomy.text: Formation of self-care skills and independence in daily activities.

social.title: Social Skills
social.text: Practicing social interactions, community rules, and appropriate behaviors.

lifeSkills.title: Practical Life Skills
lifeSkills.text: Learning competencies necessary for functional integration into family and social environments.

curriculumPage.structureParagraph1: Classes consist of 6–8 students and are coordinated by two teachers, allowing personalized intervention and consistent attention for each child.
curriculumPage.structureParagraph2: Educational activity is complemented through collaboration with specialists (counselor, speech therapist, physiotherapist), ensuring a multidisciplinary approach.
curriculumPage.evaluationParagraph1: Progress evaluation is carried out continuously through observation of individual development and adaptation of educational objectives.
curriculumPage.evaluationParagraph2: The emphasis is on real progress, measured through concrete steps toward autonomy and integration.

counselingPage.title: Counseling
counselingPage.lead: The counseling service within Rază de Soare Special School provides psychological support adapted to the needs of children with special educational requirements. The intervention aims to support emotional, behavioral, and social development within a safe and structured environment.
counselingPage.paragraph1: Counseling is an integral part of the school's multidisciplinary approach, contributing to a balance between the educational process and each child's individual needs.
objectivesList: Improvement of adaptation to the school environment
counselingPage.methodsParagraph1: Psychological intervention is carried out through individual sessions, group activities, and constant collaboration with teaching staff.
counselingPage.methodsParagraph2: The counselor works closely with the family, offering recommendations and support to ensure continuity of intervention at home.
counselingPage.roleParagraph: The counselor is part of the school's multidisciplinary team, collaborating with teachers, the speech therapist, and the physiotherapist to ensure coherent and individualized intervention.

logopediePage.lead: Speech therapy at Rază de Soare Special School is addressed to children with moderate, severe and profound intellectual disabilities, where language disorders are frequently associated with cognitive and global developmental difficulties.
logopediePage.intro: The intervention is not limited to correcting isolated sounds, as often happens in mainstream education, but focuses on developing functional communication from its basic level, starting with receptive language, compliance with simple instructions and stimulation of communicative intent.
logopediePage.contextText: A significant percentage of the students present language delay associated with intellectual disability, and many of them are nonverbal. In such cases, speech therapy aims at initiating communication and gradually building communication skills.

directions.d1: Stimulation of receptive language and understanding of simple commands
directions.d3: Initiation of speech and functional vocalizations
directions.d5: Building compliance and ability to follow instructions

logopediePage.methodsText1: Intervention includes the use of Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), pictograms, visual supports, functional gestures and other tools adapted to each child's level.
logopediePage.methodsText2: The goal is to develop the most functional form of communication possible — verbal or alternative — so that the child can express needs, preferences and emotions.
logopediePage.roleText: The speech therapist collaborates constantly with teachers, the counselor and the physiotherapist to integrate communication objectives into daily educational activities and ensure coherent intervention.

kinetotherapyPage.title: Physiotherapy
kinetotherapyPage.lead: The physiotherapy service within Rază de Soare Special School focuses on the recovery and functional development of motor abilities in children with intellectual disabilities and associated disorders.
kinetotherapyPage.paragraph1: Physiotherapy intervention supports the development of global coordination, balance, and muscle tone, contributing to increased independence in daily activities.
kinetotherapyPage.objective3: Increasing muscle tone and physical endurance
kinetotherapyPage.objective4: Developing motor skills necessary for independence
kinetotherapyPage.objective5: Preventing motor regression and associated complications
kinetotherapyPage.intervention1: Physiotherapy activities are adapted to each child's developmental level and include structured exercises for coordination, mobility, balance, and postural control.
kinetotherapyPage.intervention2: Intervention may be individual or integrated into group activities, depending on the objectives established in the individualized educational plan.
kinetotherapyPage.integration1: The physiotherapist collaborates with teachers and other specialists to integrate motor objectives into daily activities, facilitating the transfer of acquired skills into real functional contexts.
kinetotherapyPage.integration2: Motor development is closely linked to personal autonomy, participation capacity, and the child's integration into the school and community environment.
